search.description: Find anything in SWAPI whose name matches some text, across the films, characters, planets, species, starships and vehicles at once. This is how a workflow turns what a person typed into the record the other actions take, and it is the only way there is: SWAPI has no search endpoint. "Tatooine" comes back as a planet and "Millennium Falcon" as a starship without the caller having to know which is which, and every match says what it is and why it matched. No API key required.

parameters.description: The name to look for. Capitals, accents, punctuation and a leading "the" do not matter, so "the millennium falcon" and "Millennium Falcon" find the same starship. Part of a name works too, and so does a near miss.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Optional. Which collections to search. Pick any number of them; leave it empty to search all six. Narrowing it also makes the step cheaper, because SWAPI serves one file per collection and only the ones searched are fetched.

parameters.description: Optional. How many matches to return in this page. Between 1 and 100; 10 by default.

has_more.description: Whether there are more records after this page.

matches.description: The matching records in this page, best match first.

items.description: One match: what it is, what it is called, and why it matched. Pass its id or url to the Get action for its kind for the rest of it.

matched_on.description: Why this record matched: the name, the start of the name, words in the name, or being close to the name.

name.description: Its name, or a film's title.

description: Pull canonical Star Wars reference data into a workflow from SWAPI, the Star Wars API: the six films with their opening crawls, 82 characters, 60 planets, 37 species, 36 starships and 39 vehicles. Search all six collections at once to turn what a person typed into the record you need, then read that record with everything it references already resolved to names, which SWAPI itself leaves as bare URLs. Every quoted measurement comes back as a number you can compare and a phrase you can print, so a workflow can sort characters by height, planets by population or starships by cost without tripping over the strings SWAPI stores them as. No account or API key required.
